I will mainly use the land for the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the most steady way for me to earn grain yield and control risk. I know how to manage these two crops, the machines and inputs are easy to find, and with my household labor I can keep the work on time. I will plant winter wheat first and then follow with summer maize on the same fields after wheat harvest. I will not spread myself across too many crops, because I would rather keep management simple and do the key work well.

For winter wheat, I will use an improved variety because I want stable emergence, lodging resistance, and dependable yield. I will prepare the field with rotary tillage, apply base fertilizer with nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, irrigate at the critical stages, and keep pesticide use limited to the times when disease, aphids, or weeds are likely to matter. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize. I will use a hybrid maize seed because I care most about output and uniformity. I will mostly keep the soil disturbance low after wheat and use no-tillage sowing where possible, so I can save time, hold moisture, and catch the season on time. My whole plan is to keep inputs at a moderate level, protect yield, and avoid unnecessary cost.
